title: PETRACHE ET TRANCA c. ITALIE
summary: In Petrache and Tranca v. Italy, the applicants, Ms. Elena Petrache and Ms. Liliana Tranca, Romanian nationals of Roma origin, brought a case against Italy concerning their threatened eviction from a temporary accommodation centre in Rome. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Traveller families facing eviction from emergency housing, particularly when one member, Ms. Petrache, was recognised as severely disabled and dependent on daily assistance. The applicants had lived in the “Ex-Cartiera” emergency centre since 2011. In March 2016, the Rome municipality ordered them to leave as part of a broader policy to close such centres, offering alternative accommodation in the “Villaggio della Solidarietà”—a segregated site for Roma families, which the applicants refused, citing its unsuitable and discriminatory conditions. The European Court of Human Rights examined complaints under Articles 3, 8, 13, and 14 of the Convention, but ultimately declared the application inadmissible. The Court found that the applicants had not exhausted all available domestic remedies, as their legal challenge to the eviction was still pending before Italian courts. This case is significant as it underscores the procedural barriers Roma and Traveller families often face when seeking protection from forced evictions, reflecting ongoing challenges in accessing justice and adequate housing in Europe.
